1.b: There is a legend that has persisted—for decades—that net.art was first coined by Vuk Ćosić from a garbled email.

2.b: Allison Parrish launches @everyword, a Twitter poetry bot tasked with tweeting “every word in the English language, in alphabetical order, one word at a time, every thirty minutes.” The bot completed its mission in June 2014.

3.b: Aligned with previous NFT attempts by the McCoys and ascribe, DADA aimed to empower artists by enabling more people to earn a sustainable living as artists. DADA’s Creeps & Weirdos collection was launched on October 31, 2017 with a Halloween theme.

4.t: Electronic Superhighway (2016-1966) at Whitechapel Gallery, London
4.b: This major exhibition of digital art featured over 100 works exploring the impact of computer and Internet technologies on art.

5.t: Java Language Project Initiated at Sun Microsystems
5.b: In the early ’90s, Sun Microsystems began the development of the Java programming language, a watershed moment in the history of creative coding as it would be the basis for the upcoming Processing in ten years.

6.t: The Isms of Art by Hans Arp and El Lissitzky
6.b: A critical publication by the leaders of the Dadaist and Constructivist movements documenting the turbulent developemtns of the art world in the first quarter of the twentieth century.

7.t: Hermann Muthesius Founds the Deutscher Werkbund
7.b: The Deutscher Werkbund in Munich, a crucially important and influential association, aimed at improving German design and industry in global markets by partnering product manufacturers with design professionals.

8.t: Composition with Lines by Piet Mondrian
8.b: This Early Modern oil on canvas was completed during Mondrian’s transition from Cubism to Neoplasticism.A. Michael Noll in 1965 would go on to conduct a famous early computer art experiment with Mondrian’s Composition with Lines.

9.t: Joaquín Torres-García Brings Geometric Abstraction to Latin America
9.b: After forty years abroad, the Uruguayan-SpanishTorres-García brought the ideas of geometric abstraction to Latin America in order to reconcile his affinity for the movement with the region’s own cultural traditions.

10.t: Jesús Rafael Soto Settles in Paris
10.b: A seminal figure in the development of Kinetic Art, Soto’s arrival in Paris put him in contact with Victor Vasarely, Yaacov Agam, Jean Tinguely and others connected with the Salon des Réalités Nouvelles.

11.b: John McCarthy at MIT introduced the programming language LISP (List Processing) in 1960. He published the language in his seminal paper in on recursive functions in programming. LISP would go on to be used in Symbolics graphics computer.

12.b: Casey Reas’s precursor to Feral File was inspired by Harm van den Dorpel’s Left Gallery from 2015. Named a2p (artist-to-peer) and built on Bitmark with Sean Moss-Pultz, it was Reas’s early exploration of blockchain, promoting peer-to-peer art trading.

13.t: Exhibition by 31 Women at Peggy Guggenheim’s The Art of this Century
13.b: Juried by Peggy Guggenheim and Marcel Duchamp, the exhibition was one of the first at Guggenheim’s The Art of this Century.

14.b: Pythagoras credited with popularizing geometrical patterns, “the main feature of 1960s computer art. Computer artworks were frequently based on the golden section, Fibonacci numbers, and many other emblematic Pythagorean premises,” according to Grant Taylor.

15.t: Woman of War, Lady of the Wild Things by Liliane Lijn
15.b: Woman of War (1986) and Lady of the Wild Things (1983) by Liliane Lijn stand as striking testaments to the intersection of art, feminism, performance and computers during this era.

16.t: Paul Werbos Proposes Backpropagation to Train Neural Networks
16.b: In a major advancement in AI and Machine Learning research, Paul Werbos proposed using backpropagation to train neural networks at the “System Modeling and Optimization” conference in New York.

17.b: The artist describes Lorna, made from 1979 to 1984, as the first artwork to use laserdisc technology, and as an early interactive video art disc.

18.t: The Interactive Image at the University of Illinois at Chicago
18.b: Held by the Electronic Visualization Lab (EVL) at the University of Illinois at Chicago, the show lasted in installments from 1987 until 1989. A SIGGRAPH 2017 paper looked back at this event and highlighted the importance of the show in retrospect.

19.b: An important step in the rise of Mass Media Art, an important pre-condition for NFTs, according to Casey Reas, in October 1998, the MPEG (Moving Picture Experts Group) announced the MPEG-4 standard, ISO/IEC 14496, following the success of MPEG-1 and MPEG-2.

20.b: Environments, precursors to “happenings” as well as the Performance and Installation Art of the ’60s-’70s, were large-scale, immersive installations intended to engage all of the senses of the viewer.

21.b: In December, fxhash launched its long-awaited version 2.0, which incorporated Ethereum minting capabilities in addition to Tezos.Fxhash founder ciphrd spoke to this author, Peter Bauman, about the launch. Also joining were Paul Schmidt and Charlie Middleton.

22.t: Jikken Kōbō’s Fifth Presentation Introduces the Autoslide Works
22.b: As proto-video art, this exhibition was an important precursor to electronic art. It combined experimentally composed music with surrealistic visuals.

23.t: Vera Molnar Co-Founds Centre de Recherche d’Art Visuel, (later Groupe de Recherche d’Art Visuel (GRAV))
23.b: Playing a significant role in the development of Kinetic and Op Art, the Parisian collective aimed to explore the relationship between art, science and technology to create works that empirically engaged with new materials and challenged traditional notions of art.

24.t: Arturo Rosenblueth, Norbert Wiener and Julian Bigelow Publish Behavior, Purpose and Teleology
24.b: The roots of cybernetics lie uncomfortably in the terrain of autonomous weapons and the military industrial complex. After all, the ideas grew smack in the middle of WWII.

25.b: Much of this Timeline's history of AI will focus on the cybernetic-connectionist-deep learning thread. However, we will from time to time highlight major advancements in symbolic, expert systems.

26.b: While its beta debut was in late October 2021, April 2022 saw fxhash officially launch with version 1.0.

27.t: Zach Lieberman Begins Daily Instagram Animations
27.b: Like Manolo and Takawo before him, Zach Lieberman began the practice of doing daily animations on Instagram in 2016.

28.t: Suite for Five by Merce Cunningham
28.b: A hugely important moment in Chance Dance and with a score by John Cage, Suite for Five is a Neo-Dada classic.

29.t: Birth of Art Informel in France
29.b: Responding to the horrors of WWII, European artists rejected the artistic traditions of figurative and geometric work in favor of anti-compositional forms and gestural techniques.

30.b: This work, from Nees’s series exploring the polygon from 1965-1968, investigates the relationship between “order and complexity” and "aesthetic measure.”
